headline_marked: Japan pledges $295.5 million in loans, [[Bangladesh and Japan sign 6 deals]] during PM's visit
headline: Japan pledges $295.5 million in loans, Bangladesh and Japan sign 6 deals during PM's visit
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's visit to Tokyo has resulted in six bilateral cooperation agreements and significant loan pledges for development projects.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's four-day visit to Japan, starting October 26, has led to the signing of six bilateral cooperation documents, including one grant agreement.

Japan has pledged approximately $295.5 million in loans for two major projects: $100.8 million for improving the investment environment and $194.7 million for the second phase of the Upazila Management and Development Project.
A grant of up to $13.44 million has been signed to provide a patrol vessel to strengthen Bangladesh's coastal security capabilities.

Other agreements include Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) on strengthening economic relations and improving the business environment, as well as separate MoUs with Japan's Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries.
The two nations also signed an MoU on the Employment for Skill Development Program (ESDP) and a Letter of Intent (LoI) to enhance cooperation on climate change.
During the visit, the Prime Minister met with Japanese political leaders, business representatives, and development partners to discuss investment, technology transfer, and skill development.
The delegation accompanying the the Prime Minister included Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury and State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kabir.
caption:
Japan pledges nearly $300 million in loans and signs 6 key deals with Bangladesh to boost investment and security.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's four-day visit to Japan, starting October 26, has led to the signing of six bilateral cooperation documents, including one grant agreement.

Japan has pledged approximately $295.5 million in loans for two major projects: $100.8 million for improving the investment environment and $194.7 million for the second phase of the Upazila Management and Development Project.

A grant of up to $13.44 million has been signed to provide a patrol vessel to strengthen Bangladesh's coastal security capabilities.

Other agreements include Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) on strengthening economic relations and improving the business environment, as well as separate MoUs with Japan's Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries.

The two nations also signed an MoU on the Employment for Skill Development Program (ESDP) and a Letter of Intent (LoI) to enhance cooperation on climate change.

During the visit, the Prime Minister met with Japanese political leaders, business representatives, and development partners to discuss investment, technology transfer, and skill development.

The delegation accompanying the the Prime Minister included Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury and State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kabir.

headline_marked: [[IEDCR director assaulted]] in office by suspended DAB member
headline: IEDCR director assaulted in office by suspended DAB member
summary: Doctors’ Association of Bangladesh suspends a member after he allegedly assaulted the IEDCR director in his office. The organization is investigating the incident.
details: The Doctors’ Association of Bangladesh (DAB) has suspended the primary membership of Dr Zahid Hasan following allegations that he assaulted the Institute of Epidemiology, Disease Control and Research (IEDCR) director in his office. Dr Zahid, previously the assistant legal affairs secretary for DAB's central executive committee, has also been issued a show-cause notice.

The notice, signed by DAB Secretary-General Zahirul Islam Shakil, cites Dr Zahid's alleged involvement in an "unpleasant incident" at the director's office on Wednesday morning. He has been given 48 hours to explain his actions before disciplinary measures are considered.

DAB President Prof Harun Al Rashid confirmed that both the accused and the victim are members of their association. He noted that Dr Zahid had previously worked on an IEDCR project but recently lost his job, though the exact motive for the alleged assault remains under investigation.

"We are not yet certain whether this or another vested interest triggered the incident," Prof Rashid stated. "Taking the assault into account, we have suspended his membership. Further action will be taken swiftly following an investigation."
caption:
